reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing rigid positional roles with probabilistic cluster assignments. Players are no longer confined to singular roles like 'point guard' or 'center', but instead receive soft assignments across multiple clusters reflecting their multifaceted skill sets. This probabilistic framework enables a richer characterization of player utility. The derivation begins with a high-dimensional player feature space (e.g., usage rate, assist rate, rebound rate) and applies unsupervised clustering to identify latent player types. Each player receives a probability distribution over these clusters, forming a soft assignment. From this, a role vector is derived for each cluster by aggregating key statistical features. These role vectors then serve as basis elements for constructing lineup efficiency models. The model predicts net rating as a function of the interaction between these role vectors, capturing synergies or mismatches among player types. Failure modes include poor cluster separation, leading to uniform probability distributions, or misalignment between role vectors and actual game outcomes due to omitted variable bias.
